items.title: SpaceX's Starship Catch: A Reusability Milestone
points: Starship completed a 22-hour orbital mission, then flew back to its launch tower in Texas where giant mechanical arms caught it—the first-ever mechanical capture of a fully orbital rocket booster.
Booster catch itself was still unsuccessful, but the milestone brings SpaceX closer to fully reusable rockets capable of airplane-like launch frequency.
Mechanical capture avoids damage from traditional splashdown landings, cutting refurbishment time and cost.

items.title: Deadly Fungus Spreading Under Radar in Hospitals
points: A drug-resistant fungal strain was found in a Kenyan hospital patient with an infected surgical wound that resisted extensive antibiotic and antifungal treatment.
Experts suspect more cases are spreading undetected because many labs lack reliable methods to identify this specific yeast.
No established drug treatment exists; containment relies on rapid testing, patient isolation, equipment removal, and strict hygiene protocols.

items.title: Female Bonobo Hunters Reshape Understanding of Primate Behavior
points: A nine-year study of wild bonobos found females led 99 of 158 documented hunts (63%), despite males being larger and stronger.
Older, dominant females controlled meat distribution, using hunting leadership to strengthen social alliances.
Findings challenge the assumption that male-led hunting is a universal biological default among human ancestors and close primate relatives.

items.title: Historic SS United States Becomes World's Largest Artificial Reef
points: The nearly 1,000-foot transatlantic speed-record ship (built 1952) was deliberately sunk and now sits 180 feet below the Gulf of Mexico off Florida.
The $1 million project creates habitat for grouper, tuna, red snapper, and other marine species while establishing a major dive destination.
The transformation shows how retired maritime infrastructure can be repurposed for environmental restoration and recreation.

items.title: How Oakland Set a Template for AI Job Protection
points: Oakland city workers secured a tentative contract requiring the city to retrain or reassign employees displaced by AI tools, plus a 9% raise over three years.
IT worker Julian Ware warned employees could be blamed for AI errors or face increased workload without extra pay.

Other cities are following suit: Berkeley Unified requires 60 days' advance notice before AI deployment and bars using AI to evaluate workers; Columbus's transit agency needs union approval for self-driving buses; New York state law protects covered public workers from AI-driven layoffs or pay cuts.
After a year-long ChatGPT pilot, Pennsylvania is exploring how to reinvest time savings into public services, holding joint union-management discussions before deployment.

items.title: How AI Learns Like a Sleeping Baby
points: Princeton researchers fed an AI model home recordings from a baby in chronological order, but by simulated age 2 it couldn't recognize a single word.
Adding a 'replay' step at the end of each simulated day—where the AI reviewed prior days' audio—let it recognize thousands of words across eight different homes by the same age.
The technique mimics how human babies may use sleep to consolidate memories, suggesting replay prevents an AI from forgetting earlier training while learning new patterns.
This method lets researchers study how sleep aids infant learning without fully retraining the model from scratch, addressing a key challenge for continuously improving AI systems.

items.title: Major AI Funding and Product Launches
points: LangChain, a developer platform for building AI agents (software that can autonomously perform multi-step tasks), raised $300M at a $3B valuation.
OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT Wallet, letting AI agents securely pay for online purchases after user approval.
Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, two versions of the same model with different safety rules, giving users flexibility in guardrail strictness.
Google DeepMind unveiled AlphaGenome 2, which predicts how the same DNA change affects different cell types, and used AI agents to mathematically prove Signal delivers core privacy protections.
